items.title: AI-Generated Turkish Series 'Castle Walls' Launches on Prime Video in What Is Being Touted as a First
items.excerpt: AI-generated historical drama 'Castle Walls,' produced by Turkish TV powerhouse Ay Yapim, launches on Prime Video as what is billed as the first series made end-to-end with generative AI for a major streamer. It is a concrete test of whether a fully synthetic production pipeline can carry a scripted series.

items.title: After Chaos Of Cruise Vs Pitt AI Deepfakes, Seedance 2.5 Is Now Blocking Hollywood Rip-Offs
items.excerpt: ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 is now refusing prompts that reproduce Hollywood IP and star likenesses, after Seedance 2.0 triggered an outrage cycle over Cruise-vs-Pitt deepfakes. A rare look at guardrails being retrofitted into a mainstream video model creators actually use.

items.title: Former Luma AI Exec Launches L.A.-Based Production Outfit Matriarch
items.excerpt: Verena Puhm, formerly head of Dream Lab LA at Luma AI, has launched Matriarch, a Los Angeles production company built around AI-native filmmaking craft. It marks the migration of model-lab creative leads into the production side of the business.

items.title: Hollywood Makeup Pioneer Rick Baker Shares His Thoughts on AI, CGI and Stories About Eddie Murphy
items.excerpt: Seven-time Oscar-winning makeup artist Rick Baker, honored at Locarno 2026, weighs AI and CGI against practical craft and defends the below-the-line artisans he thinks go unappreciated. A veteran maker's read on what automation does to hands-on creative work.

items.title: A Filmmaker Secured a Lost Billy Joel Radio Interview. Then He Re-Created the Singer in AI
items.excerpt: A documentary filmmaker found a lost Billy Joel radio interview and used AI to reconstruct a young Billy Joel on screen — without the artist's involvement. A sharp case study in the consent gap opening up around AI-assisted documentary reenactment.

items.title: American Film Market Expands to Include AI and Tech Companies
items.excerpt: IFTA is partnering with Cannes Next on AFM House and an Innovation Hub that will put AI startups and tool vendors on the film market floor alongside sales agents. The industry's buying calendar is being restructured around production technology.

items.title: Cascadeur Ships 2026.2 with Animation Layers and 3 New Languages
items.excerpt: Nekki's physics- and AI-assisted character animation tool adds additive animation layers, easing controls, retrained inbetweening/motion-generation/retargeting networks, and a built-in MCP server that lets external AI agents drive the software. A concrete look at where neural assistance sits inside a working animation pipeline.

items.title: Bob Gaudette and Kirk Hipkiss Launch AI Film and TV Production Studio Nolia
items.excerpt: Toronto-based Nolia launches as an AI film and TV studio built around original IP, with 'The Little Cloud Thief' in development as both a feature and an episodic series. Another AI-native shop betting that owned IP, not service work, is the viable model.

items.title: Roku Created a New Channel That's Only AI Slop 24/7
items.excerpt: Roku launched Fairground AI, a 24/7 channel of exclusively AI-generated narrative shorts and commercials. No Film School asks whether there is any real audience for it, and what an always-on synthetic feed does to the value of made content.

items.title: RocXZoom Heading to Kickstarter – Robotic 50x Zoom Camera With AI Subject Tracking From Ex-DJI Engineers
items.excerpt: Ex-DJI engineers are crowdfunding RocXZoom, a robotic 50x zoom camera whose AI subject tracking handles framing and follow automatically. On-set machine vision is moving from post into the camera body itself.
